steps.goal: Read current telemetry for the 1 N thruster (P-PROP-04) to verify its health (pressure, temperature, valve status) and see if any off‑nominal trends could affect thrust capability.

Retrieve the build pedigree and flight history of thruster P-PROP-04 (including any NCRs, test results, and as-flown disposition) to assess whether the thruster can reliably deliver the required Δv for an avoidance maneuver.

Check upcoming ground contact windows and operator availability to determine if an operator can be reached before the collision avoidance deadline (closest approach in 118 min) and thus whether the burn can be executed autonomously or must be gated for operator approval.

Based on telemetry, part history, and contact analysis, propose a collision avoidance burn using the 1 N thrusters if the vehicle can perform it within the Δv envelope (≤0.5 m/s) and the operator cannot be reached in time; otherwise, propose the same burn as a gated action awaiting operator approval.

e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**: At T+2 min the FDIR event FE-201 (rule CONJ-SCREEN-PC) flagged a conjunction with Object 58321 (CDM-0412) showing a predicted miss distance of 180 m (TM-CONJ-01) and a collision probability of 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ (TM-CONJ-02), which exceeds the 1 × 10⁻⁴ action threshold. Telemetry shows the catalyst bed temperature of the 1 N thruster (P-PROP-04) is only ~20 °C (TM-PROP-05), far below the 315 °C required for firing (REQ-PROP-028). The build record NCR-002 reveals the heater was originally out-of-tolerance (52 Ω vs 46 ± 2 Ω) but was reworked before flight and closed as “Closed: reworked” with flight impact “None: preheat meets REQ-PROP-028”. Thus the vehicle is capable of reaching the needed temperature if the heater is commanded, but it is currently cold and a preheat must be initiated before an avoidance burn can be executed.

**Why the build record mattered**: The spec-sheet assumes a heater meeting the 46 ± 2 Ω limit, giving 315 °C after a 30-minute preheat. NCR-002 showed the as-built heater would only reach 290 °C in that time, blocking the thruster hot-fire until rework. Because the heater was replaced and re-tested (asFlown: Closed: reworked, preheat re-test reached 318 °C at 30 min, 12 W), the vehicle now satisfies the spec, preserving the 30-minute preheat timeline. Without this record the prognosis would incorrectly conclude the thruster cannot reach the required temperature; with it, the prognosis is that a timely preheat enables a viable avoidance burn.

**Public precedent**: WEB-1 notes that redesign of a monopropellant thruster’s catalytic bed reduced transient preheat time from 15 min to 52 s, illustrating that preheat durations can be short after design changes. WEB-2 describes preheating characteristics of an H₂O₂ monopropellant thruster, confirming that optimum preheat temperature studies are standard for ensuring efficient operation.

**For the operator**:  
*At the next pass (Svalbard, T+38 min)*  
- Authorize the collision-avoidance burn if the catalyst bed preheat has been started (requires ≤30 min to reach 315 °C per NCR-002).  
- Verify that the burn can be commanded before the T+45 min deadline and that the Δv (0.063 m/s for an 88-min lead) stays within the 0.5 m/s envelope and the remaining Δv budget (130.94 m/s left vs 120 m/s required per REQ-SYS-002).  

*Afterwards*  
- Monitor telemetry during the burn (planned start ~T+2 min + cmdT, burn duration ~32 s) to confirm thrust execution.  
- After the burn (~T+120 min, at closest approach), check TM-CONJ-01/TM-CONJ-02 for an increased miss distance and reduced collision probability.  
- Confirm post-burn thruster health via TM-PROP-05 (catalyst bed temperature) and ensure no anomalous residuals.
